title: Made to Lie Down
scripture_text: Yahweh is my shepherd; I shall lack nothing. He makes me lie down in green pastures. He leads me beside still waters. He restores my soul.
body:
"He makes me lie down." Not invites. Not suggests. Makes.

Sheep will not lie down when they are anxious. A shepherd who wants a resting flock has to deal with whatever is frightening them first — the predator in the treeline, the flies, the quarrel between two animals at the edge of the group. The rest is not laziness. It is evidence that someone competent is standing watch.

Most of us do not have a resting problem. We have a trust problem that shows up as a resting problem. We keep the phone in our hand at midnight because putting it down feels like letting go of the wheel. And then we are surprised that our soul feels thin.

David had been a shepherd before he was a king. He knew that a sheep lying down in good grass beside quiet water is a sheep that has stopped scanning the horizon, because it has learned the horizon is being watched by someone else.

Your soul gets restored in the lying down, not in the running. That is not a reward for finishing everything. It is how you were built.
discussion_questions: What are you scanning the horizon for right now?
What would it look like, practically, to let God stand watch over that today?
When did you last rest without feeling guilty about it?
activity: Pick one hour today with no screen in it. Spend ten minutes of it doing nothing at all.
